title: Three Winters and One Short Note
subtitle: 科学探索 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 科学探索（人与社会·科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）
meta: 主题语境：科学探索（人与社会·科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）　|　核心词汇：genius　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 genius 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 the teacher ① praised a genius that no examiner in the school would have described, and he said the praising was the whole of the winter. The ② genius, meaning the pupil himself and not the mark, ran three winters and stayed undescribed in the book; a genius, he said, is the only thing in a school that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ genius in that school had the same short note beside it, and the ④ genius at the far desk, meaning the one they kept for the children to copy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A genius, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the teacher said the describing is the part that fills three winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the genius was the whole of the matter, meaning the gift and not the pupil. The ⑥ genius, meaning the gift and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; genius, he said, is either something you praise or the only word that means both a pupil and a gift. He said the gift is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ genius had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short note. The ⑧ genius of the whole thing, the teacher wrote in November, was one school and three winters of describing; genius, he said, is either the one at the far desk or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ genius I remember is the one described in the plan, which closed in 1968 and is still described as the quietest in the school. A ⑩ genius, my mother said in 1970, is the only one that improves by being described; every genius, she said, is a gift that has agreed to look like a pupil. She said the gift was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 天才（指学校里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 天才（指那个学生本人，与分数相对）
C. 固定搭配：praise a genius 称赞一位天才
D. n. 天才（指留给孩子们仿效的那一位）
E. n. 天赋（抽象总称，指一所学校的天才之事）
F. n. 天才（指方案里写到、被记录过的那一位）
G. n. 天赋；才华（指一件事里人人都说却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 才华（抽象总称，指人人都说却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: praised a genius that no examiner in the school would have described
The genius, meaning the pupil himself and not the mark
the genius at the far desk
the genius was the whole of the matter
the genius had become a line in a plan
The genius of the whole thing

answers.why: praise a genius 意为“称赞一位天才”，1961 年那位老师称赞了学校里没有一位考官肯描述的一位天才。
genius 意为“天才”，指那个学生本人而不是分数，它经过了三个冬天而在簿子上没有被描述。
genius 意为“天才”，指学校里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一张矮矮的便条。
genius 意为“天才”，指最远那张课桌留给孩子们仿效的那一位，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
genius 意为“天赋、才华”，指一件事里人人都说却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份才华就是那件事的全部。
genius 意为“才华”，指人人都说却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位天才，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
genius 意为“天才”，指方案里写到、被记录过的那一位，到 1966 年这一位成了方案里的一行。
genius 意为“天赋”，老师十一月写道，整件事的天才之事是一所学校和三个冬天的描述。
genius 意为“天才”，我记得的是方案里描述过的那一位，1968 年离开了，至今仍被说成学校里最安静的一位。
genius 为抽象总称，母亲 1970 年说，一位天才是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的东西。
